replies.author: Tenthul
replies.body:
No. Until these AI tools create all of this within an engine that lets you directly edit things under the hood, this is all meaningless. As I said in another post:

An incredibly, incredibly simple game you might be able to get right in 25 prompts and a very comprehensive design doc. More like you're going to need 50 prompts for each feature, with their own comprehensive design doc. But this all misses the point. You still need a functional engine for tuning and other functional stuff. You still need to throw it into Unity or Godot or Unreal or whatever. AI should be used for making scripts, not attempts at prompting graphics + gameplay and all this "game" at once. This is why people talk about using AI to create assets (art or code or otherwise). You need assets to make a game, you might be able to make a concept, but you cant expand from that concept into a real game no matter how many additional prompts you use.

Think about the effort that goes into a simple patch for a live service game. They're little tweaks here and there, something does a little more, a little less damage, a buff lasts a little longer or shorter. These are the little details that "make a game." AI can help speed things along, but authoring real content is a boring and tedious process that requires an actual person playtesting and confirming the fun, and all of these little details are what people attempting to prompt entire games wholesale will never be able to do.

It gets nonsensical. You could say "make me a sidescrolling beat-em-up where every character can double jump and double jump kicks drop onto an enemy it does 10 damage." - done. But also you need to go into telling the AI that "Blue thug has 100 HP and does 5 damage with its kicks and 3 damage with its punches. Green thug has 200 HP and does 7 damage with its punches but cannot kick. Boss 1 has 1000 HP and knocks the player down with every hit." Like this isnt even a water droplet from an icicle at the tip of the iceberg of making a game. The context window, the tracking of information, the not-ever-losing information, and how will you ever even actually test these things to make sure they are accurate? Now you need to include debug into your prompt too.

Like, gamedev just doesn't work that way and it never will, it's not just technological iteration over time, it's an utterly flawed workflow from the start.

replies.author: Tenthul
replies.body:
I agree with you 100%. I've been copy/pasting this a lot around here these days...

  
This nonsense is just propaganda to get more people using Astra, just like after the Fable usage from Claude became available people were like "look I made shit with Fable" none of this is actual gamedev, it's people having fun with prompts and should borderline be banned content from the sub. This isn't how games are made and never will be. Yes, I know what I'm saying and no amount of "just wait a year or two." No, this is fundamentally not work that will contribute towards an actual, functional, fun, playable game outside of possibly concept work. This is not the way that AI will be able to properly assist you in making games, and anybody going down this route expecting to "make it as an indie dev" in this manner will always, always be wrong.

AI can help you make games. This is not the way to make that happen. This is a fundamentally flawed workflow at its core, not something that iteration or technological improvements can cover. Unless the intent is to be a wildly simple game.

Show me detailed, authored content. I'm not talking about art, I'm talking about numbers. Going through individual assets and tweaking numbers to get the feeling just right. AI can definitely make mass changes to these numbers easily enough, but even that requires a fundamentally different workflow than what's being shown in these "demonstrations", and what's being shown isn't something that can contribute to the former.

I am in support of AI assisted gamedev, this is nothing to rag on AI gamedev, I am talking about workflows that actually give you the end result of a functional, fun, balanced game.

This shit is meaningless propaganda intended to make people think they can do things they can't. And this is what makes people roll their eyes at AI gamedev and give it a bad impression. This is why people using AI to make real games have such an uphill battle, working to show their creation DOES in fact have soul and heart.

replies.author: lemonlemons
replies.body:
I used dream-loop skill about 5 times in a row on it (one hour runs): [https://github.com/achimala/dream-loop](https://github.com/achimala/dream-loop)

  
I edited the example prompt behind that link and asked for a first person fantasy game.

  
After first run I told Astra what I thought was wrong with the results and asked it to do another dream-loop run to fix the issues. I repeated this four times.

  
In total it cost about 50% of weekly 5x Pro usage..
